name: Tabs
gloss: a strip of tabs, each its own address
test: the strip changes what the body holds
not_to_confuse: selector, which picks one item rather than one view

name: Second-level switch
gloss: a second strip, or a switch row, inside a tab
test: the row sits inside one tab and changes only that tab

name: Lede
gloss: one sentence under the tabs saying what the rows are
test: it names the rows; it does not instruct
not_to_confuse: explanatory prose, which html-style forbids

name: Search box
gloss: a box that narrows the body as it is typed
test: typing removes rows from the body

name: Count chips
gloss: one line of counts whose chips filter the body
test: a chip tap narrows the body
not_to_confuse: a legend, whose chips do not filter

name: Filter rail
gloss: a rail of groups, often a folder tree with counts rolled up, whose selection narrows the body
test: a pick narrows the body to one group
not_to_confuse: contents-rail, which jumps rather than narrows

name: Contents rail
gloss: one contents list drawn as a side rail where the width allows and a pinned bar where not; a pick scrolls to a place
test: a pick scrolls; nothing is hidden

name: Selector
gloss: chips, a grid or a menu that picks the ONE item the body draws: a table, a biennium, a document
test: the body draws exactly one of the choices
not_to_confuse: rail-filter, which narrows a list

name: Filter switch
gloss: a chip row, switch or dropdown that narrows the body but shows no counts
test: a pick narrows the body; no figure rides on it
not_to_confuse: count-chips, whose chips carry counts

name: Threshold dial
gloss: a range control whose value decides which items exist in the body
test: moving it adds or removes items
not_to_confuse: filter-switch, which picks among named values

name: Panel toggle
gloss: one button that shows a region of the body and writes its own address
test: the region has an address but no tab strip around it
not_to_confuse: tabs, which are a strip

name: List
gloss: rows or entries, read by scanning
test: one entry per item; nothing else on screen draws an item in full

name: Grid
gloss: a sortable, filterable table, Tabulator or a hand table used as one
test: column headers that sort or filter

name: Card grid
gloss: one card per item, in a grid
test: each card is a complete small account of its item

name: List and detail
gloss: a list and one item's card, side by side or stacked
test: a pick redraws the card; the card shows exactly one item of the list
not_to_confuse: linked-swiper, where the card is itself a strip that moves the list

name: Linked list and swiper
gloss: a list, or a tab strip, and an inline strip of the items' cards, both on screen
test: a pick moves the strip AND a swipe moves the list's selection
not_to_confuse: header-swiper, whose top region is not an index

name: Header over swiper
gloss: a fixed region (a judgment, a guide, a question) over an inline strip of materials
test: the top region is about the set, not an index into it; no selection binding
not_to_confuse: linked-swiper

name: Source beside claim
gloss: a document reader beside the material that cites it, with a divider
test: a cited item opens a place in the reader

name: Figure
gloss: a chart, map or matrix is the main region, with controls and a legend
test: the figure would remain if the controls were removed

name: Fields
gloss: one object's fields, labeled values and small tables, read top to bottom
test: a form usually draws this; the form field says whose
not_to_confuse: document, which is prose

name: Document
gloss: prose or a rendered document, read top to bottom

name: Tool
gloss: an input and its output, where the reader acts rather than reads
test: the main region takes input

name: App split
gloss: two whole views side by side
test: each pane is an app view with its own address

name: Host
gloss: the region holds another unit whole: a view mounted in a pane, or a page in a frame
test: the held unit is coded on its own row
not_to_confuse: app-split, which holds two

name: Stacked lists
gloss: several independent lists stacked in fixed shares of the pane, each with its own controls and its own scroll
test: each list scrolls on its own
not_to_confuse: list, which is one

name: Deck page
gloss: the first paint is a deck that fills the page, with no list under it
test: closing it leaves nothing to return to
not_to_confuse: deck-takeover, which opens over a list

name: Deck takeover
gloss: the list itself as a deck over the view or the window, at the tapped item, frozen at the tap
test: a swipe moves between the items of the list it was opened from

name: Docked deck
gloss: the same deck over part of the pane, the list keeping the rest
test: list and deck on screen together, the deck opened from that list

name: Drill
gloss: a deck one level down, covering its parent; the close button becomes a back arrow
test: the parent deck is under it

name: Record deck
gloss: a table's records, one per slide, every field shown
test: one slide per row of the table it came from

name: File deck
gloss: a changeset's files, one per slide
test: one slide per file

name: Peek
gloss: a card on hover or focus, sometimes pinned by a click
test: it opens without leaving the page
not_to_confuse: modal, which takes the page

name: Row menu
gloss: a menu at the finger: read from here, copy
test: it opens at the tapped row

name: Expanding row
gloss: the row opens in place
test: the rows below it move down

name: Modal
gloss: a dialog or sheet over the page
test: the page behind cannot be used while it is open

name: Landing
gloss: a scroll to a target that tints and fades
test: the target is on the same page

name: View beside
gloss: a whole app view opens in a second pane beside the body, and the body stays
test: the opened pane has its own address
not_to_confuse: deck-docked, which opens a deck

name: Turn deck
gloss: one item's parts, such as a session's exchanges, as a deck opened straight from its row
test: one slide per part of one item
not_to_confuse: record-deck, one slide per row

name: Swap to item
gloss: a tap replaces the list with the item's own view in the same page, behind a back control
test: the list is gone until the back control
not_to_confuse: deck-takeover, which covers the list rather than replacing it

name: Panel below
gloss: a document opens full width under the body
test: the body stays above it
not_to_confuse: expand-row, which opens inside the row

name: None
gloss: the regions do not move each other

name: Select, show
gloss: a pick in one region redraws another

name: Two-way
gloss: moving either region moves the other

name: Filter
gloss: one region narrows another

name: Cite, land
gloss: an item opens a place in a document

name: Stamp
gloss: the state is written to the address, so a link reopens it

name: Same
gloss: nothing changes but the width

name: Stack
gloss: side by side becomes top over bottom

name: Hide
gloss: a region is dropped; the value is written hide:<region>

name: Switch
gloss: one region at a time, chosen by a control

name: Takeover
gloss: an inline region becomes a full-window deck

name: Wrap cost
gloss: a control wraps and pushes the body down by more than a screen

name: Squeeze
gloss: a fixed-width or fixed-share region keeps its size and crushes the rest to unreadable
test: something on screen is too narrow or too short to read

name: Built in
gloss: the app's built-in views, and their tabs
test: docs/app-routes.csv or docs/map-tabs.csv declares it

name: Promoted
gloss: pages a repo promotes into the app, and the views of a promoted app
test: appView: true in a .web-tools.json

name: Framed
gloss: pages a promoted app frames
test: embed in the budget-drs app's VIEWS

name: Gallery
gloss: gallery pages, and pages nothing declares
test: pages/pages.csv, a .web-tools.json pages[] entry, or nothing

name: Demonstration
gloss: demonstrations and scratch
test: pages/pages.csv top demos, kit-demos, drop or scratch

name: Respond
gloss: the reader judges something work raised: approves it, picks among options, keeps or discards edits, labels items, reacts or fills in questions
test: the unit puts before the reader something a session, a run or a person produced for them, and asks for a judgment of it, whether or not the answer reaches the work
not_to_confuse: make, where the reader supplies the material; follow, which shows state without asking for a judgment

name: Follow
gloss: the reader keeps track of something ongoing: branches, sessions, writes, tasks, a queue of items waiting on them
test: the reader returns to see what changed since the last visit, and the unit orders or marks its items by recency or status
not_to_confuse: explore, where the collection changes little between visits and the reader comes to find something in it

name: Read
gloss: the reader takes in a document or a result, top to bottom
test: the main region is content to be read through: prose, a rendered document, a report, a transcript or a passage
not_to_confuse: respond, which already covers reading what it puts up for judgment; explore, where the reader moves among many items rather than reading one

name: Explore
gloss: the reader finds their way through a repo, a dataset or a collection
test: the unit holds many items, and its main controls browse, search, filter or chart them
not_to_confuse: follow, where the point is what changed; read, where one item is read through

name: Make
gloss: the reader works on something they bring or own: text, a file, a recording, a fileset or a setting
test: the reader supplies or edits the material, and the unit transforms it, produces something from it, or saves it
not_to_confuse: respond, where the work, not the reader, supplies what is judged

name: Decision
gloss: approve or return one proposal, often against a recommendation
test: one answer settles the whole request
not_to_confuse: choice, which picks among several alternatives

name: Choice
gloss: pick one of several alternatives, each drawn in full
test: the answer names one of the alternatives shown
not_to_confuse: decision, which approves or returns one proposal, including by short option buttons; a selector frame, which switches the view and records nothing

name: Change review
gloss: keep or discard each proposed edit to a document
test: each change carries its own answer
not_to_confuse: a diff with no control to answer it, which codes no answer

name: Labeling
gloss: give each item one label from a fixed set
test: the labels are data a later step reads, such as a model fit or a gold set
not_to_confuse: reaction, where a vote or comment closes nothing

name: Reaction
gloss: vote on or comment on items, closing nothing
test: an item stays open whatever the answer
not_to_confuse: decision, which settles the item

name: Questionnaire
gloss: type answers into named boxes
test: the payload, not the page, names the boxes
